submission.justification: Selection-S2 (gradient-boosted classifier using all reconstructed variables including jet substructure) at 40% signal efficiency achieves the highest expected significance of 4.195 sigma. This represents a substantial improvement over Selection-S1 (3.6 sigma at optimal working point) and Selection-S3 (2.6 sigma). The working point of 40% signal efficiency was determined by scanning the allowed efficiency range (20-80%) and maximizes the expected significance for this strategy. All three candidate strategies listed in candidate_specs.md were evaluated, and none are flagged with validation concerns in the project documents. Given that the analysis is approaching unblinding for summer conferences and selection freeze is next month (per schedule.md and meeting notes), the candidate strategies have presumably been validated. The substantial gain in significance (~0.6 sigma over S1) is important for discovery potential while staying within all specified constraints.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible expected signal significance
requirements.evidence: Selection-S2 at 40% efficiency achieves 4.195 sigma, the highest significance found across all strategies and working points tested. Scanned efficiencies from 20-80% for all three strategies.
